title: Natural variation in OsbHLH091 fine-tunes rice floret opening time in a JAZ-mediated dance
content: Crosses between rice cultivars can produce hybrids with superior agronomic traits compared with their parental cultivars (Huang et al. 2015). However, hybridization between indica and japonica is often hindered by differences in their diurnal floret opening time (DFOT). In general, indica cultivars exhibit an earlier DFOT, typically between mid-morning to noon, whereas japonica cultivars generally open their florets 2 hours later. Understanding the mechanisms controlling DFOT is therefore important for improving hybrid rice production.
